review_notes: I read the whole file and the sibling lemmas in Comparison/Basic.lean, Comparison/TorusAction.lean and Map/Basic.lean. I compared simp attributes on the comparison lemmas (`algebraicAnalyticEquiv_smul`, `_distinguishedPoint`, `_torusι`, `_ofAffinePoint`, `analyticMap_analyticAffineChartι`, `algebraicComplexPointMap_id`, `_comp`, `_smul`). The only concrete gap I found is the missing `@[simp]` on the forward naturality lemma. I did not run Lean. I did not check whether the `erw`-style carrier mismatches stop `algebraicComplexPointMap_ofAffinePoint` from firing under plain `simp`. The suggested attribute is not tested, but I see no loop: the forward lemma moves `algebraicComplexPointMap` out of the `algebraicAnalyticEquiv` argument. The existing `_symm_naturality` rule moves it the other way, but it is stated for `.symm`, so the two rules do not rewrite the same term.

findings.excerpt:
theorem algebraicAnalyticEquiv_naturality (hΦ : Φ.IsRegular) (hΨ : Ψ.IsRegular)
    (p : Φ.AlgebraicComplexPoint) :
    Fan.algebraicAnalyticEquiv hΨ (f.algebraicComplexPointMap p) =
      f.analyticMap hΦ hΨ (Fan.algebraicAnalyticEquiv hΦ p) := by
findings.problem: The simp interface is asymmetric. The inverse form `algebraicAnalyticEquiv_symm_naturality` is `@[simp]`. The forward form is the canonical statement and is not tagged. The forward form is also the one `algebraicAnalyticEquiv_symm_naturality` uses in its own proof. Every sibling lemma that transports a structure through `algebraicAnalyticEquiv` is simp in the forward direction: `algebraicAnalyticEquiv_smul`, `algebraicAnalyticEquiv_distinguishedPoint`, `algebraicAnalyticEquiv_torusι`, `algebraicAnalyticEquiv_ofAffinePoint`. So `simp` normalises `(algebraicAnalyticEquiv hΨ).symm (f.analyticMap hΦ hΨ p)` but leaves `algebraicAnalyticEquiv hΨ (f.algebraicComplexPointMap p)` unchanged. The `_symm` proof has to go through `simpa using (…).symm` to handle it. The chart-level rule `algebraicComplexPointMap_ofAffinePoint` is simp, but the file's proofs need `erw` for the carrier mismatch (lines 60–67 and 99–102). A plain `simp` may therefore not reduce an `algebraicAnalyticEquiv` applied to an `algebraicComplexPointMap` of a general point `p`. This lemma is the only rule that handles that case.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` to `algebraicAnalyticEquiv_naturality`, so that `algebraicAnalyticEquiv hΨ (f.algebraicComplexPointMap p)` normalises to `f.analyticMap hΦ hΨ (algebraicAnalyticEquiv hΦ p)`. This matches the `_symm` rule and the torus-action siblings. The rewrite removes `algebraicComplexPointMap` from the argument of the equivalence, so I see no cycle. It does not rewrite the same term as the `.symm` rule. The `_symm_naturality` proof's `simpa using … .symm` should still work, since the added rule only rewrites the hypothesis and goal to a common form.
findings.benefit: Users get both directions of naturality by `simp`, as for torus equivariance, distinguished points and torus inclusions. They no longer need to cite `algebraicAnalyticEquiv_naturality` by hand, or use `erw` to reach the chart-level rules. The simp set for the comparison is then complete in both directions.
